memory_update.text: Stride remains the primary reference leader for K-12 virtual schooling operations, including state/district compliance, teacher staffing, curriculum, and platform execution.
Pearson/Connections Academy is a second reference anchor for full-time K-12 virtual public schools, but exposure is diluted inside a larger global education company.

Blackbaud is an underfollowed K-12 administrative software candidate: not a pure virtual-school operator, but its SIS/LMS/enrollment/billing/family-portal workflows map to the operating infrastructure needed by online and hybrid schools.
RCM Technologies is a speculative micro-cap exception tied to a regulated-input bottleneck: special education, therapy, behavioral health, nursing, and telepractice services for districts.

Many obvious K-12 virtual-school suppliers are private or recently private, including major SIS, LMS, assessment, curriculum, and teletherapy vendors; later layers should map private competitors to public substitutes and customer/supplier dependencies.

node: K-12 virtual schooling and alternative digital schooling platforms
summary: Layer 1B expands the public-company universe around the scarce operating inputs for compliant K-12 virtual schooling: full-stack online public-school operators, virtual-school curriculum/platform vendors, SIS/LMS/attendance/administrative software, and regulated special-education or teletherapy staffing. The list intentionally uses Stride and Pearson as reference anchors, then adds underfollowed infrastructure and regulated-service suppliers that could matter if virtual or alternative digital schooling scales.
